description: OpenStack Neutron DVR floating IP connectivity gap after live migration
system_prompt: You are a senior systems engineer with deep expertise in Linux internals, distributed systems, networking, and infrastructure operations. Think through the problem carefully — consider all interacting mechanisms before committing to an answer. Show your reasoning chain explicitly before stating conclusions.
user_message:
An OpenStack deployment uses Neutron with DVR (Distributed Virtual Router) and
ML2/OVS. An instance with a floating IP (FIP) is live-migrated from Compute
Node A to Compute Node B. The migration completes successfully per nova-compute
and Neutron logs. No errors are reported.

After migration, approximately 30% of external clients experience a 45–60 second
connectivity gap before traffic to the FIP resumes. The remaining 70% of clients
see no interruption. The instance itself responds immediately when directly reached.

(a) Identify the exact mechanism causing the 45–60 second gap. Trace the path
    from FIP relocation to the specific network device that is serving stale
    forwarding state, and name the timer or aging mechanism responsible.
(b) Explain why only 30% of clients are affected while 70% are not, despite all
    clients targeting the same FIP.
(c) Describe the correct fix at each relevant layer: Neutron configuration,
    OVS, and the physical network. For each layer, state what the fix does and
    why it is necessary.
